title: Two Sum
statement:
You are given an array of n integers and a target value. Exactly one pair of distinct positions in the array adds up to the target. Print the two positions.

Positions are 0-based. Print the smaller position first.
inputFormat:
Line 1: the integer n, the length of the array.
Line 2: n integers, the array.
Line 3: the integer target.
outputFormat: One line holding the two 0-based positions, smaller first, separated by a single space.
constraints: Exactly one pair of positions adds up to the target
sampleNotes: The values at positions 0 and 1 are 2 and 7, and 2 + 7 is 9.
The values at positions 1 and 2 are 2 and 4, and 2 + 4 is 6. Position 0 is not part of the answer.
hint: The largest tests have n = 200000. Checking every pair is twenty billion comparisons and will not finish in time, in any language. One pass with a hash map from value to position will, because it looks at each element once.

starter.py:
import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
a = [int(x) for x in data[1:1 + n]]
target = int(data[1 + n])

# Your code here. Print the two 0-based positions, smaller first.
